result.title: TransHarness: From Benchmark Overfitting to Transferable Harness Evolution
result.comment: 22 pages, 8 figures, including references and appendices
result.summary: Harness evolution offers a path to improving coding agents without updating model weights. However, existing methods can overfit their evolution benchmarks, producing gains that fail to carry over to new tasks. To address this challenge, we introduce Transferable Harness Evolution (TransHarness), which evolves harness intervention policies from same-task success-failure contrasts. These policies couple execution-context triggers with diagnostic guidance, enabling task-dependent checks and corrections beyond the source executions. Cross-task replay and independent semantic selection retain policies that intervene selectively and ground corrections in current-task evidence rather than source-specific solutions. We further curate an independent evolution set for cross-distribution transfer and conduct a cross-benchmark evaluation covering multiple strong models and a range of lightweight and mature harnesses. Experiments show that, with only 300 source trajectories from outside the test distribution, TransHarness further improves strong agents across distinct target benchmarks, demonstrating transferable harness evolution beyond benchmark overfitting. Specifically, TransHarness achieves state-of-the-art scores of 76.4% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 95.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, surpassing the strongest baseline model, GPT-6 Astra, by 2.4 and 5.6 percentage points, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TransHarness，从同任务的成败轨迹对比中演化出带触发条件与诊断指引的 harness 干预策略，并通过跨任务回放与语义筛选缓解基准过拟合，在编码 agent 基准上验证迁移效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是编码 agent 的外部 harness 提示与干预策略演化，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、证据获取与内部表示，失败对比与选择性干预的线索与本主题联系过弱，难以构成具体借鉴。
